answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The velvet multiplier is published, charged in saffron, and horizon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4357 identities would post 1500 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
